tools.name: inspect_payment
tools.description: Use this when the user wants to check a proposed payment against explicit rules before sending it, for example whether the amount, recipient, asset or network matches their policy or would exceed their limit. Compares the proposal with the user's structured policy and returns ALLOW, REQUIRE_APPROVAL

tools.name: get_receipt
tools.description: Use this when the user has an exact public OCD receipt ID (OCD-RCP-...) and wants to see the recorded evidence, for example what a payment receipt contains. Requires the exact receipt_id; it cannot search or list receipts, and has no payment, publication or private-operation access. Returns the unch

tools.name: verify_receipt
tools.description: Use this when the user wants to know whether an OCD receipt proof is valid, for example whether a receipt is authentic or its evidence signature checks out. Returns VALID, INVALID or UNVERIFIABLE for one public receipt_id OR an envelope the user may share with OCD, without credentials or payment aut

tools.name: create_payment_receipt
tools.description: Use after a supported payment has occurred to independently observe its exact network and transaction reference and create or return a signed OCD receipt. findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: inspect_payment · Private data: inspect_payment, get_receipt, verify_receipt, create_payment_receipt · Public sink: inspect_payment, verify_receipt.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: inspect_payment · Private data: inspect_payment, get_receipt, verify_receipt, create_payment_receipt · Public sink: inspect_payment, verify_receipt

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
